label_basis: Internal back-office, so not a Digital Service. Payroll + NRIC + bank files reads as Confidential/Sensitive High. Hosting is never stated (vendor-customised since 2016), and the type turns entirely on it: medium-risk-cloud if cloud, low-risk-on-premises if not. Cannot be narrowed further from the text.

External supplier-facing transactional service on government commercial cloud (hosting stated). WOGAA tracking not mentioned, so whether it counts as a Digital Service is unresolved; 1,400 suppliers is far under 1M either way. ACRA certs and financial statements read as Restricted rather than Confidential.

Main public website, so a Digital Service. 200,000 visits/month = 2.4M/year, clearly over the 1M threshold, making it High Impact. Content is public announcements and forms, so the hosting tier underneath is low. Hosting hedged ('I think it's on the government cloud?') but the DSS answer does not depend on it.

Public licensing service with Singpass auth on GCC AWS — both a Digital Service and a cloud system holding personal data. 40k applications/year is stated but visits are not, so the 1M DSS threshold is not directly answerable; applications-to-visits is plausibly under. Payments hand off to the WOG gateway so card data is out of scope.

Internal enforcement case management holding NRIC, addresses and complainant identities — Confidential/Sensitive High. Not CII. Hosting never stated (built ~2014, replacement mooted), so the same cloud/on-prem fork as EV-001 applies and cannot be resolved.

Cloud is unambiguous (S3, Redshift, Airflow). Untokenised NRIC in the raw layer reads as Confidential/Sensitive High. That satisfies wizard q5's literal 'Confidential/Sensitive High AND cloud-hosted' clause, which routes to high-risk-cloud — but high-risk-cloud is the CII profile and a reporting warehouse is not CII. Both readings are defensible; this is exactly the q5 compounding defect in F-004.

Primarily an internal officer tool (ArcGIS Enterprise) with a cut-down public viewer that is secondary, so not principally a Digital Service. Land parcels and asset locations read as Restricted. Hosting explicitly unknown to the describer ('where exactly the tile server sits I'd have to check').

Water level and flow monitoring on pump houses could be utility infrastructure, which raises a real CII question the text cannot settle. Platform is vendor-run and the describer explicitly does not know the architecture, so hosting is unknown too. Widest acceptable set in the pilot — deliberately, because the description genuinely does not narrow it.

Internal EDMS holding official records, contracts and minutes under a classification scheme — Restricted to Confidential. 'SharePoint based' does not disambiguate hosting: SharePoint runs both as M365 cloud and on-premises, and the text does not say which.

Internal staff intranet: announcements, forms, directory, room and shuttle booking. Sensitivity is clearly low — the only case where that is unambiguous. Hosting again unresolved ('Runs on SharePoint'). Shortest description in the set at 31 words.

Cloud is stated ('Genesys, the cloud version'). Call recordings plus interaction history against identified callers push toward Confidential/Sensitive High, but retention is vague ('we keep them for a period') and the content is service enquiries rather than case data, so low-risk is defensible. Agent-operated, not a public Digital Service.

Public mobile app with Singpass login, so a Digital Service. 40k monthly actives sits right against the 1M visits/year line depending on sessions per user — genuinely undecidable from the text, which is the point. Saved vehicle and property details are personal but not obviously Confidential. Parked accessibility work is directly relevant to the WCAG-heavy DSS domains.

Adversarial by construction. Literally a staging environment, which routes to sandbox at wizard q4 — but the anonymisation script has been failing silently since June, so it holds live citizen data. Sandbox is 3 mandatory controls plus 114 optional; applying it here would be badly wrong on substance. The correct answer arguably depends on data, not environment label. Ordered with medium-risk-cloud first deliberately.

RAG assistant over internal circulars and SOPs — GenAI is the core function. The compound case: composition is permitted but not required (F-002), so generative-ai alone is defensible and generative-ai plus a hosting profile is too. Hosting is hedged ('Azure OpenAI I believe, or the government's own service now'). Staff-only pilot of 200, so arguably nonprod as well.

Billing and payments handling $18M/year across 90k transactions. Card and eNETS go through a gateway under Finance's merchant account, so card data is out of scope here. Invoice and GIRO data still reads as Confidential/Sensitive High. Hosting never mentioned — same unresolved fork.
